messages.body_plain:
Thanks, you were right.

I used to do the same, but I came up with problem, that data doubles. If I deploy app from one directory (/home/adomas/apps/), then it copies everything connected to it to /srv/shiny-server/. I do the following for deployment

sudo cp -R /home/adomas/apps/ /srv/shiny-server/

On Friday, May 30, 2014 8:19:20 PM UTC+3, Andy Kipp wrote:
> I think the issue is that you are referencing the directory "../data". Only sub directories of your application directory are uploaded to ShinyApps.
>
> If your application code is in "/path/to/my_app", then you should move the data directory to "/path/to/my_app/data" and re run deployApp()
>
> Hope that helps.
> -Andy
>
>
> On Fri, May 30, 2014 at 10:12 AM, Adomas Budrys <adomas...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I was developing shiny app locally and after deploying it on server it came up with an error. I got the following error:
> >
> > The application unexpectedly exited.
> > Diagnostic information has been dumped to the JavaScript error console.
> >
> > That was interesting error I have never had it before, therefore I have checked what's wrong on JS console and I found:
> >
> > Listening on http://127.0.0.1:33494 <http://127.0.0.1/> Shiny URLs starting with /progress will mapped to /usr/lib64/R/library/shinyIncubator/progress Shiny URLs starting with /progress will mapped to /usr/lib64/R/library/shinyIncubator/progress Error in if (file.info <http://file.info>(paste(directory, country, "_useless.csv", : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
> >
> > In the application I have a separate file, which is used for user to store some data. User can add or delete, therefore in the beginning, application checks if file is not empty (this is where it fails) and in this case gives a value NULL, otherwise reads the file and stores data from file.
> >
> > The following is beginning of code from server.R where crashes:
> >
> > directory <- ".../data/"
> > country <- "usa"
> >
> > shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
> >
> >   # Reads .csv, which stores data
> >   if (file.info <http://file.info>(paste(directory,country,"_useless.csv",sep=""))$size == 0) {
> >     blackBox2 <- NULL
> >   }
> >   else {
> >     uselessRead <- read.table(paste(directory,country,"_useless.csv",sep=""),header=FALSE)
> >     blackBox2 <<- as.vector(uselessRead[,1])
> >   }
> > ....
> >
> > However, it is strange, that nothing after "_useless.csv", is read, therefore I couldn't find out why it doesn't work.
> >
> > If anyone has any ideas, please share it.
> >
> > Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Error: cannot open the connection
messages.body_plain:
Kevin,

Unfortunately ShinyApps doesn't do a great job of exposing the log files from running shiny applications. This is something that I think we are going to work on in the coming months. In the meantime, I took a look for you and the output is attached. I think the problem is that you are trying to read a file from your "Dropbox" directory, which is not available on the ShinyApps servers. You should move these files into the same directory as your application/documents so they get deployed when you call deployApp().

Cheers,
-Andy

messages.body_plain:
Account names can not be changed. However you can go to https://www.shinyapps.io/register and create a second account with whatever name you like. You will then have to register your account by running. Using your existing token and secret.

shinyapps::setAccountInfo("new account", token=... , secret=...)

deployApp(account="new account")

Cheers
-Andy

Logging in to ShinyApps will then prompt to select a gmail account.

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
Authentication in ShinyApps is tied to your Google account. A google account can not be associated with more then one ShinyApps user. However, a ShinyApps user can have more then one Account (think of Accounts as similar to organizations in GitHub).

For example:

I have a ShinyApps user (an...@rstudio.com) tied to my Gmail account (also an...@rstudio.com).

However my user has multiple ShinyApps accounts:

andy.shinyapps.io <http://andy.shinyapps.io>
andy2.shinyapps.io <http://andy2.shinyapps.io>
demos.shinyapps.io <http://demos.shinyapps.io>
gallery.shinyapps.io <http://gallery.shinyapps.io>

I can deploy to any of these accounts by running:

deployApp(account="andy2")

Because of this feature, there is no reason to have more then one ShinyApps user (but it is possible if you have more then one Gmail account).

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

We have deployed a test version of an app in shinyapps. The application works correctly in our web explorer but not in a client's network. There, the application takes a lot more time to run and, on top, maps using rCharts library are not showing (they appear gray). The rest of the app works correctly (simple graphs and graphs using rCharts). Could this be a problem with proxy configuration when downloading the map? The maps come from Open Street Maps.

Has anybody seen this problem / something similar or suspects what can be going wrong?

thanks,

Franco

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] reactiveValues on shinyApps
messages.body_plain:
Josh, I think I know what this is. If you add this to your app:

output$debuginfo <- renderPrint({
  str(reactiveValuesToList(input))
})

and a corresponding verbatimTextOutput("debuginfo") in ui.R, I think you'll find that when run on ShinyApps.io there are a couple of "hidden" inputs that are being sent along and included in your input object. So you'll either have to remove these values from x, or construct x explicitly by grabbing the pieces you want from input rather than converting the whole thing.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Special Characters
messages.body_plain:
Karl,

We're in the process of figuring out what is going on with non-ascii encoded files, as another user has reported similar problems.

My theory is that your source/data files are encoded in ISO-8859/Windows 1252, which R we're not able to decode (they should be encoded in UTF-8).

./funktionen.R:     UTF-8 Unicode text, with CRLF line terminators
./gametable.csv:    ISO-8859 text, with CRLF line terminators
./manifest.json:    ASCII English text, with very long lines, with CRLF line terminators
./player.csv:       ASCII text, with very long lines, with CRLF line terminators
./read_html.R:      ISO-8859 text, with CRLF line terminators
./server.R:         ISO-8859 text, with CRLF line terminators
./test_read_html.R: ISO-8859 text, with CRLF line terminators
./ui.R:             UTF-8 Unicode text, with CRLF line terminators

Can you send the output of sessionInfo()?

Thanks
-Andy

messages.subject: Re: Trouble deploying app that uses the 'tm' package
messages.subject_clean: Trouble deploying app that uses the 'tm' package
messages.body_plain:
I have managed to answer my own question - ShinyApps is running instances of R 3.03 and the 'tm' package I am dependent on (v0.6) requires R v3.1. I cured the issue by 'rolling-back' the version of 'tm' that I was using to v0.5-10.

I'm not sure if this is the most elegant solution to the problem - I'd be interested to hear of better ways around the issue.

I'm writing my first shiny app. The purpose is very simple : The user gets 6 numbers and he has to fill in the average. Cause I'm working in Belgium we use comma as decimal.   cannot open file '12': No such file or directory
Error in file(file, "r") : cannot open the connection

It seems gsub is looking for a file????

How can i get this to work properly?

best regards,
Gunther

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] What are the limitations of 'instances'?
messages.body_plain:
The answer to your question about how many users an instance can support is "it depends". An instance is virtual server dedicated for a particular application. The number of users an instance can support depends on the workload of the application. Since R is a single-threaded process, if a particular application is doing heavy computation other users will be forced to wait before their requests can be processed. Likewise, if the application is doing relatively little computation, many users can be serviced by a single R process.

To work around this limitation of R, ShinyApps can scale both the number of R processes per instance, and the number of instances. However, as you noticed, these feature are not enabled for the Alpha. If you are running into issues with application performance because of many users, I can work with you to address this.

Hope that helps,
-Andy

messages.subject: deployApp not working and creating huge files on harddrive
messages.subject_clean: deployApp not working and creating huge files on harddrive
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am using the latest shiny version on RStudio 0.98.932 on Mac OSX 10.9.3.

I want to report a very strange behaviour of the deployApp function. When I deploy an app as a R markdown with shiny runtime, I have the following message :

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...

Nothing special yet. However, the uploading process actually never stops. One hour later, I noticed that my hardrive was full.

After inspection, it turned out that the uploading process created 350 Go of files in the following directory : /private/var/folders/2m/_qvzrlqx7893wm2c0ykpjm9w0000gn/T//Rtmpoi9oBa/file1697660e7edd

This duplicated my 'downloads' and 'documents' folders dozens of times in this directory, until there was no space available.

This must come from shinyapps since I have the following warnings after a while :

Warning messages:
1: In file.append(to[okay], from[okay]) : write error during file append
2: In dir.create(dirname(to), recursive = TRUE) :
  cannot create dir '/var/folders/2m/_qvzrlqx7893wm2c0ykpjm9w0000gn/T//Rtmpoi9oBa/file1697660e7edd/Documents/MyFolder', reason 'No space left on device'
3: In file.create(to[okay]) :
  cannot create file '/var/folders/2m/_qvzrlqx7893wm2c0ykpjm9w0000gn/T//Rtmpoi9oBa/file1697660e7edd/Documents/MyFolder/Example.twb', reason 'No such file or directory'
4: In dir.create(dirname(to), recursive = TRUE) :
  cannot create dir '/var/folders/2m/_qvzrlqx7893wm2c0ykpjm9w0000gn/T//Rtmpoi9oBa/file1697660e7edd/Documents/MyFolder', reason 'No space left on device'
5: In file.create(to[okay]) :
  cannot create file '/var/folders/2m/_qvzrlqx7893wm2c0ykpjm9w0000gn/T//Rtmpoi9oBa/file1697660e7edd/Documents/MyFolder/Example.twb', reason 'No such file or directory'
6: In dir.create(dirname(to), recursive = TRUE) :
  cannot create dir '/var/folders/2m/_qvzrlqx7893wm2c0ykpjm9w0000gn/T//Rtmpoi9oBa/file1697660e7edd/Documents/MyFolder', reason 'No space left on device'

This behaviour happens consistently when I launch the deployApp function. As of yet it is impossible for me to deploy a R markdown to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, and I have to clean up the junk files caused by this bug every time I try to deploy.

Could you please have a look at this ? You will find attached a sample R markdown code generating this error on my system.

Thanks,
Simon

Hope that helps,
-Andy

Hello,

I encountered a problem somewhat similar to Juan's one: when I deployed my app with shiny 0.9, it worked, but threw an error popup about misformed JSON when I read and displayed (with renderDataTable) CSV files with non-ASCII character. The CSV files and all the files of the shiny app are encoded in UTF-8, and the app sets the locale of the server to fr_FR.UTF-8.
Otherwise, the app works perfectly fine both locally (Ubuntu) and on my server with Shiny server open source (Ubuntu as well, see http://www.joelgombin.fr:3838/shiny/LireMinInterieur/).

So I tried to upgrade shiny to 0.10, hoping that it would work better on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. But now, it doesn't work at all, it seems that non-ASCII characters crash shiny all along: I get an 'unexpected INCOMPLETE_STRING' error, see https://gombin.shinyapps.io/LireMinInterieur/.

Any idea what may be going wrong? The sourcecode of the app can be found here: https://github.com/joelgombin/LireMinInterieur/tree/master/inst/liremininterieur

Thanks!

Joel

messages.body_plain:
Folks,

I apologize this error message is a little confusing. What it is saying here is that your application name in invalid. Application names must be at least 3 characters, and may NOT contain spaces. . By default application names are the name of the directory you are deploying. To work around this, you can either a) rename your application directory, or b) call deployApp(appName="my-app-name")

Hope that helps.

Evan,

I am not sure what the the exact problem is here, but it from the looks of it, it seems there is a syntax error in your requirements.R file. Please keep in mind that all files in the application directory are uploaded and parsed when you call deployApp(), so they must not have any syntax errors. deployApp() by default uses the current working directory.

-Andy
